criteria: PR #14931 and the backfill are merged into master, visible in the public repository.
The rule set is extended with lookalike-address matching (prefix and suffix comparison, including previous native transfers) and token-imitation detection, each with tests in the public repository.
The database schema, realtime processing of new transfers, and the backfill job are in place, and the backfill is validated by a load test at Ethereum mainnet scale.
Past Ethereum mainnet token transfers are backfilled, checked by the technical reviewer against the public API.
A precision report on a labeled sample of at least 100 flagged transfers is published in the repository, with the labeled list.
milestones.name: Tuned detector with backfill

criteria: Flagged addresses are reported to the Metadata microservice. Mimic addresses are tagged as phishing and transaction issuers as scam, shown by the public tag on a live Blockscout instance.
The poisoning field and its environment variables are documented in the public docs repository, for Ethereum and the L2s Blockscout hosts.
QA and staging results at mainnet scale are published, covering realtime fetcher performance and database load.
milestones.name: Public API and Metadata reporting

criteria: An integration guide and a reference example are published in the public docs repository.

At least 3 wallets outside Blockscout run the API in production for Ethereum or L2 transfers, one of them must be: Ledger, Rabby, Rainbow, Keeper, Ambire, MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Safe, each shown by a public announcement, a merged pull request, or confirmation from the technical reviewer.
Blockscout provides engineering support to each integrating wallet through production launch.
A maintenance plan committing at least 5 engineering hours per month is published in the repository.
milestones.name: Outside wallet adoption

sections.commitments:
- The current Blockscout repository license applies.
- Blockscout maintains the feature set after the money is spent, committing at least 5 engineering hours per month from paid API plan revenue.
- New requests are funded by the projects that ask for them.
sections.in_scope:
- Tune rule weights and thresholds on a labeled sample, and publish precision.
- Harden the realtime fetcher and backfill past transfers.
- Report flagged addresses to the Metadata microservice.
- Document the public `poisoning` field for Ethereum and the L2s Blockscout hosts.
- QA and staging at mainnet scale.
sections.out_scope:
- Chains other than Ethereum and its L2s.
- Wallet interfaces, which integrators build.
- Blocking or reversing transfers.
sections.team: Blockscout does the work: Victor Baranov, lead engineer; Nikita Savik, product and API manager; Nick Zenchick, DevOps; Tom Goriunov, front end; Yan Yaskov, Lead QA. Track record: [Victor](https://github.com/vbaranov), [Nikita](https://github.com/NikitaSavik), [Nick](https://github.com/nzenchik), [Tom](https://github.com/tom2drum), [Yan](https://github.com/yvaskov), [Blockscout](https://github.com/blockscout/blockscout). No other funder pays for this scope.
sections.why: Address poisoning plants dust transfers from look-alike addresses in a victim's history, hoping they copy the wrong one. Scam Sniffer tracked a $50 million loss in December 2025 and a $12.2 million loss in January 2026 ([Cointelegraph](https://cointelegraph.com/news/over-62m-lost-address-poisoning-since-december-scam-sniffer)). Blockscout offers only an admin-managed scam badge today. Afterwards, any wallet can check an address against a public score before a user sends funds.
sections.why_grant: [PR #14931](https://github.com/blockscout/blockscout/pull/14931) is a working draft: a weighted rule engine, a realtime indexer fetcher, a storage table, a `poisoning` field on API v2 token transfers, and tests. It lacks a backfill and Metadata reporting, so this ask covers tuning, backfill, reporting and adoption.

initiative.summary: Blockscout scores every token transfer for address poisoning and serves the score through a public API. A working draft is open as PR #14931. This grant funds tuning, a backfill, Metadata reporting, and outside wallet adoption.
initiative.title: Blockscout: Address Poisoning Detection and Public API for Ethereum and L2s
